text.p: Electropure Inc on Monday said it has tentatively settled a $3 million default judgment against the company, its unit HOH Intl Inc and current and former company officers.

The suit was filed in February 1993 by the Economic Development Bank for Puerto Rico, HOH's preferred stockholder, but defendants were not notified until October 1996, after the judgment had been entered, Electropure said in a statement.
The settlement calls for Electropure to issue to the bank 100,000 common shares and 100,000 five-year warrants to acquire shares, exercisable at $1.00 per share.
The company also will pay the bank $12,000 to cover certain costs and attorneys' fees.
The settlement requires Electropure to conclude talks with EDI Components over the termination of licensing arrangements between the companies established in 1992.
The judgment also was directed rendered against HOH/CNM2 Enterprises and its incorporators, including Radames Torres, the former president and general manager of HOH.
The suit had alleged breach of fiduciary duty in entering into a distribution agreement with HOH/CNM2 Enterprises which ultimately led to the dissolution of the subsidiary.
